newsitem.title: GERMANY: German businessman still missing after ransom paid.
newsitem.headline: German businessman still missing after ransom paid.

text.p: A Frankfurt businessman was still missing on Saturday two days after his brother paid a four million mark ($2.62 million) ransom to kidnappers, German police said.
Jakub Fiszmann, a 40-year-old businessman, was kidnapped on October 1, police said after lifting a local news blackout on the crime.
"We assume that the victim is still alive," said police spokesman Klaus Timm.
Officials believe that he is being held, perhaps in a subterranean hideout, somewhere near Frankfurt.
Police said Fiszmann was attacked and pushed into a van on the street in front of his company's office in Frankfurt at around 10.30 p.m. on October 1.
The businessman, who runs a property and electronics company in Frankfurt, apparently tried to fight off his kidnappers.
His broken wristwatch and small amounts of blood stemming from a struggle were later found in a white van police say was used for the kidnapping.
Fiszmann's brother paid the four million mark ransom, as the kidnappers had demanded, on Thursday. But they did not release Fiszmann as promised, the authorities said.
The four million mark payment was dropped off along a motorway north of Frankfurt on Thursday. Police did not provide any further details about the ransom payment.
Police said that the last time they had received any signs that the millionaire businessman was still alive was on October 2 when his voice was heard in a telephone message.
Authorities suspect that the kidnappers may be part of the same group that unsuccessfully tried to extort money during the aborted kidnapping of Fiszmann's nephew in 1991.
The nephew, who was six years old at the time, was released three days after he was kidnapped.

State police director Juergen Noeckel told a news conference in Wiesbaden on Saturday that there were certain details in a letter from the kidnappers in this case that could only be known to the 1991 kidnappers.
Fiszmann is known locally for financing the production of the musical "Tommy" in Offenbach near Frankfurt. ($1=1.5293 Mark)
